subject: Post-event synthesis, timeline, actions and evidence request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-event synthesis, timeline, actions and evidence request

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the patience while we ran the internal review. Attached is a concise synthesis of what we found during the August 2nd event that affected inference availability for a subset of your production routes. This message summarizes the causal findings, a short event timeline, planned corrective actions with owners, and the evidence we can provide for your audit team.

TL;DR (short summary):
- Root cause: misrouted fallback policy + KV-cache eviction race during a capacity transition, which allowed a small fraction (~0.7%) of active sessions to experience state loss and token-generation retries.
- Impact window: ~2026-08-02T14:03:12Z to 2026-08-02T14:24:47Z (21m35s); impact concentrated on europe-west-1 serving group during an autoscale burst.
- Customer-facing actions: confirmed token replay detection, restored session continuity for affected sessions, and a config patch to routing-failsafe applied 2026-08-03 02:10 UTC.

What we are sharing with you in this thread (attachments/links below):
1) event timeline (CSV) with per-route request identifiers and timestamps (nimbuspay_event_timeline.csv).
2) evidence bundle: kernel logs, autoscaler decision traces, and hashed request ids for verification (evidence_bundle_checksums.txt).
3) our remediation plan and owners (remediation_plan_v1.pdf).

Action items we are committing to (owners & ETA):
- Diego Fernandez (Engineering): implement an additional guard in the routing-failsafe to prevent simultaneous fallback and cache-swap (eta: 2026-08-11).
- Monica Patel (Customer Success): run a verification session with your SREs and share acceptance checklist (eta: coordinate this week).
- Aditya Rao (Sales/Eng): review contractual impact and propose a goodwill credit once verification completes (eta: 2026-08-06).

Questions we have for you (short):
- Would you like per-request hashes redacted before we share the CSV internally within your org?
- Do you prefer a short technical verification call (30m) or a walk-through session (60m) with our engineers?

I appreciate the frank feedback from Jacob and your ops team during the incident. We want to make sure the evidence we send is useful for NimbusPay's compliance reviewers; if you need anything additional (packet captures, extended logs), tell us and we'll prioritize.

Attachments:
- nimbuspay_event_timeline.csv (summary table)
- evidence_bundle_checksums.txt (sha256s for evidence files)
- remediation_plan_v1.pdf (action ledger, owners, mitigations)

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference  |  Developer-first inference runtime for production workloads
From: Lena Park <lena@nimbuspay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-event synthesis, timeline, actions and evidence request

Aditya — thanks for the quick synthesis and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions from our ops desk before we route this to compliance: 

1) The timeline CSV — does it include full request bodies or only identifiers/hashes? We need identifiers only for internal verification; compliance will request anonymized hashes.
2) Can you confirm whether any customer data was ever written to persistent disks during the event window? Our preliminary read suggests no, but we need confirmation for our SOC checklist.

Also, on credits: we appreciate the offer. Could you share the standard calculation you use for goodwill credits (is it pro-rated for impacted tokens or a flat service credit)? Our procurement team (cc Jacob) will want the approach documented.

We'd like to do a 30-minute verification call if possible — Wed 08/05 09:00 PT works for our team. Please confirm who from Redwood will join.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Head of Ops — NimbusPay
lena@nimbuspay.com
Phone: +1 (212) 555-0108
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:20:03 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed mitigations + verification plan (for customer call)

Aditya / Monica — draft notes (internal) to prep for the verification call with NimbusPay tomorrow: 

- Short explainer: during autoscale, routing-failsafe attempted to reroute traffic to a compatible instance class but the KV-cache eviction completed at approximately the same time; under a narrow timing window the reroute executed before the cache warm-up completed which caused a small set of sessions to re-initialize (lost prefix state). That led to token-generation retries and short-lived 5XX responses until clients retried.
- Mitigations we propose to present:
  * Immediate: enabled stricter ordering in rollout (already applied 2026-08-03 02:10 UTC) + explicit TTL bump for KV cache seeds (complete).
  * Near-term dev fix: atomic route-update + cache-swap gate (Diego, eta 2026-08-11).
  * Long-term: add per-session replay-detection and persistent session checkpoints (backlog item Q4).

Evidence we can bring to the call: condensed request timeline (rows show only timestamp + route + hashed request id), autoscaler decision log snippets, and sanitized logs showing the cache eviction event.

For the credit calculation — my recommendation: base on duration-weighted affected throughput rather than raw tokens. That maps better to how this was surfaced and avoids over-penalizing minor retries. Aditya, happy to help draft the formula for procurement.

Fyi Diego: please prepare a short 3-slide tech deck to show the cache/routing timeline and the planned code-level guard. We'll keep it high-level for SREs.

Thanks,
Dylan
Director, Trust & Safety (internal)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Jacob Meyer <jacob.meyer@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 13:42:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-event synthesis, timeline, actions and evidence request

Hi Lena / Jacob —

Thanks for the questions. Short answers up front:
- The CSV we shared contains only minimal identifiers (request_id, route, timestamp) and hashed request ids for verification; no request bodies or PII. We can additionally redact the hashed ids per your preference before we upload to your internal Drive.
- We confirm no customer data was written to persistent disks during the window. The evidence bundle includes mount logs and process traces showing in-memory cache churn only.

Call: Wed 08/05 09:00 PT works — we'll join with a small team: Diego (Engineering lead), Monica (CS lead), and me. We'll keep it to 30 minutes. 

Credit approach: our proposal is a single-line goodwill credit calculated as: (measured impacted throughput fraction) x (average daily bill for the affected routes) x (impact duration ratio). Dylan will draft the exact formula and include a worked example for your procurement team. We can provide that in writing after the verification call.

Next steps (for now):
- I will upload a redacted CSV and the evidence checksum file to the Drive link below before EOD PT today.
- Diego will prepare the 3-slide deck (technical timeline + fix plan).
- Monica will send a 1-page acceptance checklist for your SREs to sign off after the verification session.

Drive link (restricted): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/event-evidence
DocuSign (remediation acknowledgement): https://redwood.app/docusign/NP-46-remediation

We appreciate the constructive collaboration — we'll see you tomorrow on the call.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Aditya on behalf of Redwood Inference — we take operational reliability seriously and will support NimbusPay through verification and acceptance
